about: A named intermediate that writes key: none pairs nothing, so every record of its dataset matches every current row (LOOKUP-5, #4271). Selection and absence then answer as for any lookup: one record is read by every row, no record gives the absence answer, missing when none is declared, or fails under require_match (LOOKUP-24), and two records fail as multiple_matches unless order_by and keep choose one, whatever order they are stored in (LOOKUP-10). Every value is authored from those rules. key: none is refused where it cannot mean every record: on a pair relation, whose key pairs its two sides (LOOKUP-27), on a row driver, which declares no key (ROW-2), and on an aggregate, whose key admits no none (SCHEMA-12).
